newsitem.title: USA: Dozens file tobacco lawsuits in central Florida.
newsitem.headline: Dozens file tobacco lawsuits in central Florida.

text.p: Dozens of lawsuits seeking damages from tobacco companies for smoking-related illnesses have been filed in central Florida courts, with one law firm alone filing more than 80, the Orlando Sentinel reported Monday.

"We think things are changing," Glen Mayfield, the Ormond Beach lawyer who filed the suits, told the newspaper, referring to the tobacco industry's record of never paying damages in 40 years of liability suits.
He said his firm has filed more than 38 cases in Volusia County, four in Lake County, 10 in Orange County, two in Osceola County, 13 in Seminole County and six in Brevard County.

Analysts have said they expected Florida would see more of the suits, following a judgment last summer in a Jacksonville court awarding $750,000 in damages to a man who claimed he had been sickened by cigarettes. That case is being appealed.

Attorneys for tobacco have responded by filing motions in one Lake County case arguing that the suits should be handled in federal rather than state court because damages, if awarded, would be more than $75,000 and because the companies named are not Florida corporations.
